commonMerchantRebuttals: The customer agreed to recurring billing terms
The account remained accessible after renewal
Cancellation was not completed under the merchant's process
strategyTips: Pin the timeline to the exact cancellation request and renewal date
Show that any cancellation flow was hidden, broken, or confusing
Demonstrate that the customer did not use the service after the disputed renewal
evidenceToFocusOn: screenshots of subscription settings and cancellation flow
usage logs showing no post-renewal activity
subscription.customerStrategy: Frame the dispute around cancellation timing, lack of post-renewal benefit, and any merchant friction that prevented a clean cancellation.

commonMerchantRebuttals: The traveler accepted the fare or lodging rules
The service was available even if the customer chose not to use it
strategyTips: Separate non-use from non-delivery and focus on what the merchant failed to provide
Capture schedule changes, cancellations, or substitute services that materially altered the booking
Use booking confirmations and policy snapshots from the purchase date
evidenceToFocusOn: policy language in effect on the purchase date
travel.customerStrategy: Travel disputes are strongest when they show a concrete service failure, a material change, or a promised refund that never posted.

commonMerchantRebuttals: The content was delivered or accessible
The account shows logins or downloads
Digital sales were final under the merchant's policy
strategyTips: Challenge access logs when the account holder never successfully used the product
Distinguish a failed login or broken activation from valid delivery
Document defects, missing features, or an inability to access the purchased item
evidenceToFocusOn: support tickets showing activation or login problems
merchant product promises captured at checkout
digital-goods.customerStrategy: For digital goods, prove either that access never truly worked or that the product materially failed to match what was promised.

commonMerchantRebuttals: The customer received access to the program
The service was delivered as described
The agreement disclaimed results and refunds
strategyTips: Separate access from delivery of the promised service scope
Compare the sales claims to what was actually provided session by session
Preserve refund requests and merchant responses that admit delays or omissions
evidenceToFocusOn: messages requesting delivery, cancellation, or refund
coaching.customerStrategy: Coaching disputes work best when the evidence shows a gap between the promised scope and the actual service delivered, not just dissatisfaction with results.

commonMerchantRebuttals: The seller fulfilled the purchase by transferring admission rights
strategyTips: Focus on invalid, unusable, or undelivered tickets rather than a general refund desire
Document venue notices, event cancellation details, or transfer failures
Preserve order history and support responses from both the platform and the seller
evidenceToFocusOn: proof that the ticket barcode or admission credential failed
event-tickets.customerStrategy: Ticket disputes are strongest when they show the buyer did not receive valid admission rights or the event materially changed or failed.

commonMerchantRebuttals: The seller fulfilled the order and the marketplace only facilitated the transaction
The platform's internal case process was not completed
strategyTips: Keep seller conduct and platform responses separate in the evidence timeline
Show every attempt to resolve through the marketplace's internal process
Highlight platform messages, seller promises, and delivery inconsistencies side by side
evidenceToFocusOn: internal case or claim records from the platform
marketplace.customerStrategy: Marketplace disputes need a clean chronology showing what the seller promised, how the platform responded, and why the final outcome still failed the buyer.
